subject: MAP and billing guardrails for NovaRetail pilot
messages:
From: Emma Green <emma.green@novaretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>; procurement@novaretail.com
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novaretail.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot MAP: clarification on ramp caps & burst fees

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is aligned to move forward with the 90-day evaluation. Before we finalize the MAP and SOW, procurement asked for a couple of clarifications on billing that will determine whether we sign the pilot amendment this month: 

- We need a clear definition of "burst"/overage pricing vs. steady-state overage. How is burst measured (concurrent GPU, TPS, or token-rate)?
- Can you confirm whether there is a soft-cap during the initial ramp (first 30 days) and, if so, whether overage will be capped or billed at a reduced rate?
- We also need the latest rate card and a draft of the MAP milestones so our finance team can sanity-check internal budgets.

Procurement has attached the scope document they prefer we reference in the SOW. Ideally we can get a short note of proposed guardrails (billing language) that procurement can use verbatim in the amendment.

Appreciate a fast turnaround — our procurement goal is to complete signoff by EOD Friday.

Best,
Emma Green
Director, Platform Partnerships
NovaRetail

Attachments: NovaRetail_pilot_scope.pdf (application/pdf, 86KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Green <emma.green@novaretail.com>
Cc: procurement@novaretail.com; Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novaretail.com>; laura_bennett@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP: clarification on ramp caps & burst fees

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Glad to hear the team's ready to move. I pulled the key pieces into a short MAP draft and attached our current rate card for transparency. See highlights below and a proposed contract-friendly clause you can paste into the amendment: 

Summary (proposal)
- Evaluation period: 90-day pilot; target go/no-go milestone at day 60 based on latency and cost-per-inference KPIs in the MAP workbook attached.
- Commit & discount: NovaRetail commits to a 12k CPI (compute-instance) equivalent commit during pilot to qualify for a 12% pilot discount on hosted inference unit pricing.
- Burst/overage definition: "Burst" is any sustained usage above the committed throughput sustained for >5 minutes or total monthly tokens exceeding commit by >20%. Overage = requests that exceed commit under either criteria.
- Ramp buffer (first 30 days): Overages during days 1–30 will be billed at 50% of the standard overage rate up to a safety ceiling of 20% of committed monthly spend. Any usage beyond that ceiling reverts to standard overage pricing.
- Canary/rollback: We recommend a 14-day canary for new routes; if you prefer 7 days we can accommodate but will flag in the MAP.

Attachments included: redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf, NovaRetail_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook with milestones & success criteria).

Next steps
1) If procurement agrees to the ramp buffer + 20% ceiling we can produce a contract amendment for signature (DocuSign).
2) Laura (cc'd) will confirm final billing language and any absolute monetary cap we can offer for the pilot.
3) Rishi (cc'd) will confirm legal/discount approval if we need to adjust the % discount.

Quoted for context: 
> On Thu, Apr 1, 2026 at 9:15 AM Emma Green <emma.green@novaretail.com> wrote:
> > Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is aligned to move forward with the 90-day evaluation...

Thanks — I can turn this into an amendment today once procurement confirms the ceiling.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 210KB); NovaRetail_MAP_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommended billing language and cap for NovaRetail pilot

Quick internal note to align before we send a final amendment to NovaRetail: 

- Ramp buffer approach is fine, but recommend tightening: make the initial "grace" window 14 days (instead of a full 30) billed at 50% of the standard overage rate; then apply the 20% safety ceiling for the remainder of the month. Keeps our exposure bounded and gives customer breathing room.
- For legal/finance comfort, propose an absolute dollar ceiling for the pilot month(s): $30,000 absolute cap on billable overages for the pilot period. If customer crosses that ceiling, further usage is subject to prior written approval or automatically migrated to a dedicated capacity rate card.
- Billing clause (suggested wording): "During the thirty (30) day ramp window, Customer's billable overage will be billed at fifty percent (50%) of the standard overage rate until the Safety Ceiling (20% of committed monthly spend, or $30,000, whichever is lower) is reached. Thereafter, overages will be billed at the standard overage rate unless Parties agree in writing to alternate terms."

Attachment: billing_playbook_notes.txt (text/plain, 4KB)

If you want to be aggressive on the discount to close this quarter, we can offset part of the risk by shortening the ramp buffer and keeping the absolute cap. Happy to discuss phone.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Green <emma.green@novaretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaretail.com; Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novaretail.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP: clarification on ramp caps & burst fees

Soojin — appreciate the fast follow and the workbook. Procurement reviewed the proposed language and the team is comfortable with the ramp buffer + 20% ceiling, but we need the absolute dollar cap in writing. We can accept the $30,000 absolute overage cap for the pilot as Laura suggested.

Two small asks before we sign: 
1) Can the canary window be set to 7 days instead of 14? That helps us validate routes faster.
2) Please add the absolute dollar cap into the amendment body (we'll need it verbatim for procurement).

If you can send the amendment with the suggested clause and a DocuSign link, procurement will route for signatures today. HubSpot deal link attached for your team reference.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot on the books.

Emma Green
Director, Platform Partnerships
NovaRetail

Attachments: procurement_signoff_req.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 24KB)
